title: Case study: Anthropic Scion, not a migration recommendation
summary: Study a workload-specific design choice without copying its scale assumptions.

claims.text: Anthropic reported moving its monorepo to the in-house Scion system and explicitly said it is not a general-purpose Git replacement.

levels.overview: State the reported problem and the bounds of the comparison.
levels.architecture: Compare the source-control client/server split and the resulting review/CI obligations.
levels.detail: Ask which original constraints apply to our own repositories before suggesting any change.

example.input: An authored comparison checklist for our present Git workflow.
steps: Compare a small change to existing Git tooling.
Retain the status quo unless evidence justifies more.
example.output: An explicit no-migration default for this campaign.
limits: No Scion software, benchmark, connector or repository migration is supplied.
Do not confuse it with GoogleCloudPlatform Scion, SCION networking, or Scion Asset Management.

alternatives.label: Existing Git plus focused improvements
alternatives.whenToConsider: The default here unless a measured bottleneck warrants change.

alternatives.label: Study specialized source-control designs
alternatives.whenToConsider: Research only; no assumption that an internal implementation is available or suitable.

interview.question: Which assumptions would have to hold before you copied this case study?
answerHints: Separate reported results from your own measurements.

instanceMappingPolicy: An explicit source-pinned link is required; names, icons and tags are not evidence.
